title: Childproofing the Home
hook: Anchoring furniture and TVs is the childproofing step parents skip most — and tip-overs are one of the deadliest home hazards for young kids. Then you cover the rest and redo it as baby gets mobile.
key_points: Anchor dressers, bookcases, and TVs to the wall — unsecured furniture and TVs tip over and seriously injure or kill young children.
Cover unused outlets, put gates at the top and bottom of stairs, and tie up or cut loop window-blind cords.
Lock cleaners, medicines, and detergent packets up high and out of sight, and set the water heater to a safe temperature to prevent scald burns.
Childproofing isn't one-and-done — get down to your child's level and redo it each time they reach a new stage of crawling, cruising, and climbing.
content_html: If you do one thing first, anchor the furniture. Unsecured dressers, bookcases, and TVs are among the deadliest hazards in a home with young children — the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's Anchor It! campaign exists precisely because these items tip over onto kids who climb or pull on them. Inexpensive straps or brackets fasten them to the wall, and TVs are safest anchored or set on low, stable furniture.
extra_html: From there, work down the list: cover unused electrical outlets, put gates at the top and bottom of stairs, and tie up or cut the loops on window-blind cords. Lock cleaners, medicines, and laundry detergent packets up high and out of sight, and set your water heater to a safe temperature so taps can't scald. The trick is that childproofing is never finished — get down to your child's eye level and redo your sweep each time they start crawling, cruising, and climbing. This is general guidance — take a hands-on infant first-aid/CPR class, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

source.name: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (Anchor It!)

related.title: Poison and Medicine Safety
related.hook: Most poisonings happen with a parent home but distracted. Store medicines and cleaners locked, up, and in their original containers — and save Poison Control: 1-800-222-1222.

related.title: Water Safety
related.hook: Drowning is fast and silent — no splashing, no shouting. The single best protection for a young child is an adult within arm's reach whenever there's water.

flashcards.prompt: Which childproofing step targets one of the deadliest home hazards but is most often skipped?

choices.text: Anchoring dressers, bookcases, and TVs to the wall
Putting non-slip mats in the bathtub

flashcards.explanation_html: The CPSC's Anchor It! campaign exists because unsecured furniture and TVs tip over onto children — anchoring them is a high-impact, often-missed step.

flashcards.prompt: Why is childproofing not a one-time job?
flashcards.back_html: A baby's reach and skills keep changing. As they learn to crawl, cruise, and climb, new hazards come within reach — so you get down to their level and redo it at each stage.
